hints: Look carefully at what D means in this Venn. It is the very centre where saturated triglyceride, collagen and haemoglobin all overlap, so ask yourself if each one on its own has 3 or more double bonds.

Remember where C=O double bonds hide: each ester bond in a triglyceride has one, each peptide bond in a protein has one, and the haem group in haemoglobin has many C=C and C=N double bonds in its ring.
walkthrough:
**Decode the Venn diagram**

Think of each circle as a group of molecules. Region D is the middle overlap, so it means molecules that are true for all three circles: saturated triglyceride AND collagen AND haemoglobin.

To pick D, we must prove all three types contain at least three double bonds.

**Count double bonds in each molecule**

A saturated triglyceride has 3 fatty acids joined to glycerol by 3 ester bonds. Each ester bond contains one C=O double bond, so that is 3 double bonds already.

Collagen and haemoglobin are both proteins with hundreds of amino acids joined by peptide bonds. Each peptide bond contains one C=O double bond, so they have far more than three. Haemoglobin also has 4 haem groups, and each haem porphyrin ring is full of alternating double bonds.

**Choose the region that fits all three**

Since saturated triglyceride, collagen and haemoglobin all have at least three double bonds, the correct region must include all three circles.

That is only the central overlap, region D.

options.A: Region A is only the overlap of saturated triglyceride and haemoglobin. It leaves out collagen, but collagen also has many C=O double bonds in its peptide bonds, so this is incomplete.
options.B: Region B is only the overlap of collagen and haemoglobin. It leaves out saturated triglyceride, but a saturated triglyceride still has 3 C=O double bonds in its 3 ester bonds, so this is incomplete.
options.C: Region C is only the overlap of saturated triglyceride and collagen. It leaves out haemoglobin, but haemoglobin also has many double bonds in its peptide bonds and haem groups, so this is incomplete.
options.D: Region D is the centre where all three overlap. All three molecule types have at least three double bonds from ester C=O, peptide C=O, and haem ring double bonds, so D is correct.
